I’m an old hand at this now, so I won’t do anything fancy. On my wheat-maize land, I’ll mostly follow the way that has kept the family steady: put the better land into wheat and summer maize, and keep some land in cotton for extra cash. Money is still important, so I won’t chase the highest input. If I spend too much on fertilizer and water, then there’s no cushion left at home. But I also don’t dare cut too hard, because if wheat turns yellow or maize gets weak after emergence, the loss is bigger than the money saved. So this year I’ll keep inputs in the middle, use the well when the crop really needs it, and rely on family labor where I can.
